markers.impact: Reduced Diamine Oxidase (DAO) activity
markers.interpretation: The AOC1 rs10156191 T allele is associated with lower DAO enzyme production. DAO is the primary enzyme responsible for breaking down ingested histamine in the gut. T-carriers may experience elevated sensitivity to high-histamine foods.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Gut microbiome, inflammatory bowel conditions, and DAO inhibitors (alcohol, certain medications) play a massive role in actual histamine tolerance.

sources.name: AOC1 gene variants and diamine oxidase activity
sources.notes: Identifies promoter SNPs associated with decreased DAO expression.

markers.impact: Reduced Histamine N-Methyltransferase activity
markers.interpretation: HNMT is responsible for intracellular histamine breakdown, particularly in the brain. The Thr105Ile T allele reduces enzyme activity, potentially prolonging intracellular histamine signals in the central nervous system.
confirm_with: symptoms of central histamine sensitivity (congestion, headaches)
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Overall histamine load (including DAO status and mast cell degranulation) dictates central nervous system symptoms.

sources.name: HNMT Thr105Ile polymorphism impact on enzyme function
sources.notes: Demonstrates reduction in thermal stability and activity of the HNMT 105Ile isoform.

markers.impact: Lactase gene promoter downregulation (Lactose Intolerance)
markers.interpretation: MCM6 regulates the LCT (lactase) gene. Homozygous C/C results in adult lactase non-persistence (lactose intolerance) in European populations. T-carriers (C/T or T/T) maintain lactase expression throughout adulthood.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Specific to European ancestry; lactase persistence in other regions is driven by distinct MCM6 variants.

sources.name: MCM6 promoter mutations regulating LCT expression
sources.notes: Identifies the upstream promoter mutation responsible for lactase persistence.

markers.impact: Reduced aldehyde dehydrogenase 2 activity / acetaldehyde accumulation
markers.interpretation: The ALDH2 rs671 A allele markedly reduces ALDH2 enzyme function. Carriers can accumulate acetaldehyde after alcohol exposure, producing flushing, tachycardia, nausea, headache, and higher alcohol-related tissue-stress risk when alcohol is consumed.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Most consumer files can call rs671, but symptoms depend on alcohol dose, ADH1B status, medications, liver function, and ancestry background.

sources.name: ALDH2 rs671 and alcohol flushing/acetaldehyde
sources.notes: Reviews the inactive ALDH2 rs671 variant as a driver of alcohol flushing through acetaldehyde accumulation.

markers.impact: Faster ethanol-to-acetaldehyde conversion / alcohol response modifier
markers.interpretation: The ADH1B rs1229984 T allele encodes the His48 ADH1B*2 form, which increases ethanol oxidation to acetaldehyde. It is often associated with lower alcohol intake and alcohol-use-disorder protection, but can intensify acetaldehyde burden when ALDH2 clearance is weak.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Interpret together with ALDH2, alcohol exposure, sex, body size, liver function, and cultural drinking context.

sources.name: ADH1B rs1229984 and alcohol dependence
sources.notes: Identifies rs1229984 as a coding ADH1B Arg48His variant associated with alcohol dependence phenotypes.

sources.name: ADH1B/ALDH2 alcohol-related disorder and cancer risks
sources.notes: Examines combined ADH1B rs1229984 and ALDH2 rs671 effects in alcohol-related outcomes.

markers.impact: Caffeine metabolism and inducibility modifier
markers.interpretation: CYP1A2 rs762551 is commonly used as a caffeine-clearance and CYP1A2 inducibility marker. The A allele is often treated as the inducible/fast-metabolism allele, but the effect is context-dependent and modified by smoking, hormones, liver status, and habitual caffeine use.
do_not_claim: fast caffeine metabolism under all conditions
markers.raw_dna_limitation: This marker should not be interpreted with a simplistic fast/slow binary; CYP1A2 is environmentally inducible.

sources.name: CYP1A2/ADORA2A caffeine pharmacogenetics review
sources.notes: Reviews CYP1A2 and ADORA2A effects on caffeine behavior and response.

markers.impact: Adenosine receptor sensitivity / caffeine sleep-anxiety response
markers.interpretation: ADORA2A rs5751876 modifies sensitivity to caffeine's wakefulness-promoting, anxiogenic, and sleep-disrupting effects. It is most useful when interpreted alongside caffeine timing and CYP1A2 status.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: The signal matters most under caffeine exposure; no-caffeine nights may show little or no phenotype.

sources.name: ADORA2A genetic variation and caffeine/sleep
sources.notes: Reviews ADORA2A rs5751876 and caffeine-related sleep characteristics.

markers.impact: FUT2 non-secretor status / mucosal glycan and B12 context
markers.interpretation: FUT2 rs601338 A/A produces non-secretor status for many individuals, altering ABO antigen secretion into mucosal fluids. Non-secretor status can influence norovirus susceptibility patterns and is associated with differences in measured vitamin B12 fractions.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: FUT2 effects vary by pathogen strain, ancestry, ABO type, microbiome, and the B12 biomarker being measured.

sources.name: FUT2 rs601338 and vitamin B12 fractions
sources.notes: Reports FUT2 rs601338 p.Trp154Ter association with haptocorrin-bound vitamin B12.

sources.name: FUT2 common variants and plasma B12
sources.notes: GWAS association between FUT2-region variation and plasma vitamin B12.

markers.impact: HFE-related iron overload susceptibility when homozygous or compound heterozygous
markers.interpretation: HFE rs1800562 A encodes C282Y, the major common HFE hemochromatosis variant. Homozygous C282Y has the strongest common genetic association with iron overload, but penetrance is incomplete and phenotype must be confirmed with iron studies.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Genotype alone does not establish iron overload. Ferritin and transferrin saturation determine phenotype.

sources.name: HFE-Related Hemochromatosis GeneReviews
sources.notes: Clinical reference for HFE-related hemochromatosis, C282Y/H63D interpretation, and incomplete penetrance.

markers.impact: Mild HFE iron-loading modifier, especially with C282Y
markers.interpretation: HFE rs1799945 G encodes H63D. Alone it usually has low clinical penetrance, but it can modify iron loading when combined with C282Y or relevant clinical context.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: H63D is common and usually not sufficient for clinical hemochromatosis without phenotype or compound heterozygosity.

sources.name: HFE-Related Hemochromatosis GeneReviews
sources.notes: Clinical reference for C282Y/H63D genotype interpretation and penetrance.

markers.impact: Reduced MTHFR activity / homocysteine context marker
markers.interpretation: MTHFR rs1801133 T reduces MTHFR activity, especially in T/T individuals. Its practical value is as a folate/B12/riboflavin/homocysteine context marker, not as a standalone disease explanation.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Folate intake and lab values matter more than the genotype alone; common MTHFR variants are heavily overclaimed online.

sources.name: CDC MTHFR gene variant and folic acid facts
sources.notes: CDC states people with MTHFR variants can process folic acid and emphasizes folic acid intake over genotype.

markers.impact: Mild MTHFR activity modifier / one-carbon metabolism context
markers.interpretation: MTHFR rs1801131 G has a smaller and more context-dependent effect than C677T. It should be treated as a weak one-carbon metabolism context marker, especially when combined with C677T and actual homocysteine/folate/B12 labs.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: A1298C is commonly overinterpreted; do not infer disease or supplement requirements without labs.

sources.name: CDC MTHFR gene variant and folic acid facts
sources.notes: Use as a guardrail source against common MTHFR overclaims.

markers.impact: Methionine synthase reductase / B12-dependent methylation context
markers.interpretation: MTRR regenerates active methionine synthase, linking B12 status to homocysteine recycling. rs1801394 G has been associated with altered homocysteine in some cohorts, but effects are inconsistent and lab-dependent.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: This is a weak-to-moderate context marker; labs and diet dominate interpretation.

sources.name: MTRR A66G and homocysteine
sources.notes: Early study reporting MTRR A66G influence on circulating total homocysteine.

sources.name: MTRR/MTR polymorphisms and B-vitamin interaction
sources.notes: Shows MTRR/MTR effects are context-dependent and modified by B-vitamin factors.

markers.impact: Methionine synthase / B12-dependent homocysteine recycling context
markers.interpretation: MTR rs1805087 is a common methionine synthase variant studied in one-carbon metabolism. Evidence for individual prediction is inconsistent, so it should only be used as a weak context marker alongside B12, folate, and homocysteine labs.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Published findings are heterogeneous; do not score this as a strong causal marker.

sources.name: MTR A2756G and homocysteine context
sources.notes: Reviews one-carbon polymorphisms including MTR A2756G.

sources.name: MTR A2756G original plasma marker study
sources.notes: Original MTR A2756G study did not find strong differences in folate/B12/homocysteine, supporting conservative interpretation.

markers.impact: Transcobalamin transport variation / active B12 context
markers.interpretation: TCN2 transports the active fraction of vitamin B12 to tissues. rs1801198 G has been associated with B12-related biomarkers in some studies, but it should be interpreted only with measured B12, methylmalonic acid, and homocysteine.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: This is not a standalone B12-status test; diet, absorption, intrinsic factor, medications, and gut disease can dominate.

sources.name: TCN2 rs1801198 and vitamin B12 markers
sources.notes: Reports TCN2 c.776G>C association with vitamin B12 status markers.

markers.impact: Phosphatidylcholine synthesis / choline requirement context
markers.interpretation: PEMT rs7946 influences endogenous phosphatidylcholine synthesis and has been studied as a modifier of choline requirement and hepatic fat risk. Treat as a nutrition-context marker, especially when dietary choline intake is low.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: PEMT effects differ by sex, estrogen status, diet, and liver-metabolic context.

sources.name: PEMT rs7946 and choline/hepatic steatosis
sources.notes: Reports sex-specific effects of PEMT rs7946 on choline requirement and hepatic steatosis risk.

sources.name: Common polymorphisms and human choline requirements
sources.notes: Controlled feeding work showing common choline-pathway variants can affect choline requirement.

markers.impact: Omega-3/omega-6 long-chain PUFA conversion context
markers.interpretation: FADS1 rs174547 tags fatty-acid desaturase activity differences affecting conversion of shorter-chain polyunsaturated fats into long-chain omega-3/omega-6 derivatives. Useful for diet context, not as a disease claim.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Effect directions can vary by haplotype and ancestry; use as a desaturase-context flag rather than a standalone nutrition prescription.

sources.name: FADS1 rs174547 and long-chain PUFA levels
sources.notes: Analyzes effects of FADS1 rs174547 on long-chain PUFA levels.

sources.name: FADS1 rs174547 and PUFA biomarkers
sources.notes: Reports FADS1 genotype effects on PUFA blood levels.

markers.impact: Vitamin D receptor protein-length/activity variation
markers.interpretation: VDR rs2228570 (FokI) changes the VDR start codon region and can alter receptor activity. It is useful only as a vitamin-D signaling context marker alongside measured 25(OH)D and clinical phenotype.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: VDR genotype does not replace 25(OH)D testing and should not dictate dosing by itself.

sources.name: VDR polymorphism overview
sources.notes: NCBI gene summary for vitamin D receptor function and regulatory roles.

sources.name: VDR FokI rs2228570 review context
sources.notes: Recent study context for VDR rs2228570 and vitamin D deficiency/susceptibility associations.

markers.impact: Vitamin D receptor regulatory variation / bone-mineral context
markers.interpretation: VDR rs1544410 (BsmI) is a noncoding VDR marker often studied with other VDR variants for bone, immune, and vitamin-D-response context. It should be treated as a weak modifier rather than a direct deficiency marker.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: This marker has heterogeneous associations across cohorts and should not override lab testing.

sources.name: VDR polymorphisms FokI/BsmI/ApaI/TaqI context
sources.notes: Studies multiple VDR polymorphisms including BsmI rs1544410.

markers.impact: Insulin secretion / type 2 diabetes susceptibility
markers.interpretation: TCF7L2 rs7903146 T is one of the most replicated common type 2 diabetes susceptibility alleles and appears to affect insulin secretion/incretin biology. Use as a metabolic-risk context marker, not a diagnosis.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Absolute risk depends heavily on body composition, diet, exercise, sleep, age, and family history.

sources.name: TCF7L2 and type 2 diabetes review
sources.notes: Reviews TCF7L2 as a robust type 2 diabetes susceptibility locus.

sources.name: TCF7L2 rs7903146 and incretin/insulin secretion
sources.notes: Reports rs7903146 effect on T2D risk in part through incretin-related insulin secretion.

markers.impact: Satiety/appetite and adiposity predisposition
markers.interpretation: FTO rs9939609 A is a replicated obesity/adiposity-associated allele. In core interpretation, treat it as a satiety, energy-intake, and weight-management context marker, not as destiny.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: FTO effects are modest and often blunted by exercise, protein/fiber intake, sleep quality, and food environment.

sources.name: FTO rs9939609 appetite/satiety response
sources.notes: Reports role of FTO in responsiveness to hunger and satiety cues.

sources.name: FTO rs9939609 and loss-of-control eating
sources.notes: Associates FTO risk alleles with eating behavior in youth cohorts.

markers.impact: Melanocortin appetite signaling / obesity susceptibility
markers.interpretation: MC4R rs17782313 C is a replicated common marker near MC4R associated with higher obesity susceptibility and eating-behavior differences. Interpret as appetite/energy-balance context only.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: MC4R common markers have modest effects and are strongly modified by environment and behavior.

sources.name: MC4R rs17782313 and obesity risk meta-analysis context
sources.notes: Reports association between MC4R rs17782313 and obesity risk.

sources.name: MC4R rs17782313 and eating behavior/hormonal factors
sources.notes: Studies rs17782313 with behavioral and hormonal factors in obesity context.

markers.impact: PPAR-gamma insulin sensitivity and adipocyte differentiation context
markers.interpretation: PPARG rs1801282 G encodes the Ala12 form. Many studies treat it as a metabolic-response modifier related to insulin sensitivity, adipocyte biology, and diet interactions, but results vary by ancestry and phenotype.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Associations are heterogeneous; use as a weak metabolic-context marker, not a standalone prediction.

sources.name: PPARG Pro12Ala common variant review
sources.notes: Reviews PPARG Pro12Ala metabolic associations and heterogeneity.

sources.name: PPARG2 Pro12Ala diet interaction context
sources.notes: Describes Pro12Ala as C>G coding/missense variant and diet interactions.

markers.impact: Zinc transporter 8 / insulin granule biology and T2D risk
markers.interpretation: SLC30A8 rs13266634 C is the common Arg325 allele associated with higher type 2 diabetes risk in multiple studies, likely through beta-cell zinc transport and insulin processing context.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: The effect is modest; metabolic phenotype and lifestyle factors dominate absolute risk.

sources.name: SLC30A8 rs13266634 C allele and T2D risk
sources.notes: States the common C allele is associated with increased type 2 diabetes risk.

sources.name: SLC30A8 rs13266634 meta-analysis
sources.notes: Meta-analysis supporting association of C allele carriers with T2D risk.

markers.impact: Hepatic fat accumulation and fatty-liver severity modifier
markers.interpretation: PNPLA3 rs738409 G encodes I148M and is one of the strongest common genetic modifiers of fatty liver susceptibility and progression risk. Use with liver enzymes, metabolic status, alcohol exposure, and imaging.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Genotype is not diagnosis; phenotype requires liver labs/imaging and alcohol/metabolic context.

sources.name: PNPLA3 rs738409 C>G and hepatic fibrosis/HCC risk
sources.notes: Review/meta-analysis context for PNPLA3 rs738409 and hepatic fibrosis/HCC risk.

sources.name: PNPLA3 rs738409 and NAFLD histologic injury meta-analysis
sources.notes: Meta-analysis showing strong influence of PNPLA3 rs738409 on fatty liver and histologic injury.

markers.impact: Local T4-to-T3 conversion modifier / thyroid hormone signaling context
markers.interpretation: DIO2 rs225014 A encodes the Ala92 form and has been studied as a modifier of intracellular T3 production and levothyroxine response in some cohorts. Interpret only with thyroid labs and symptoms.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Evidence is mixed; clinical thyroid management should be based on labs, symptoms, and clinician guidance, not genotype alone.

sources.name: DIO2 Thr92Ala physiology review
sources.notes: Reviews DIO2 physiology and polymorphisms including Thr92Ala.

sources.name: DIO2 and persistent symptoms in LT4-treated patients context
sources.notes: NCBI gene record summarizes current literature links for DIO2 polymorphisms and thyroid phenotypes.

markers.impact: Common autoimmune susceptibility marker
markers.interpretation: PTPN22 rs2476601 A encodes the R620W allele, one of the stronger common autoimmune susceptibility variants in European ancestry populations, including thyroid autoimmunity, type 1 diabetes, and rheumatoid arthritis contexts.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Autoimmunity is polygenic and environment-modified; absence of this allele does not reduce clinical symptoms or family history.

sources.name: PTPN22 R620W autoimmunity review
sources.notes: Reviews PTPN22 R620W as a common autoimmunity susceptibility variant.

sources.name: PTPN22 Gene NCBI
sources.notes: NCBI gene record summarizing PTPN22 immune function and disease associations.

markers.impact: Mitochondrial antioxidant transport/activity context
markers.interpretation: SOD2 rs4880 alters the mitochondrial targeting sequence of manganese superoxide dismutase. The T/Val allele is often interpreted as a modifier of mitochondrial antioxidant handling, but clinical effects are heterogeneous.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: This is a mechanistic modifier, not a diagnostic marker; phenotype depends on mitochondrial load, inflammation, diet, and exercise.

sources.name: SOD2 Ala16Val mitochondrial targeting review
sources.notes: Reviews rs4880 Ala16Val structural effects on mitochondrial targeting domain.

sources.name: SOD2 Ala16Val mutation structural study
sources.notes: Discusses Ala16Val effects on SOD2 secondary structure.

markers.impact: Selenium-dependent glutathione peroxidase activity modifier
markers.interpretation: GPX1 rs1050450 T encodes the Leu198 form and has been associated with reduced GPx1 enzyme activity in some studies. Useful as a selenium/antioxidant context marker, not as disease prediction.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: GPX1 activity depends on selenium status and broader redox biology; genotype alone is weak.

sources.name: GPX1 Pro198Leu and reduced enzyme activity
sources.notes: Reports T allele association with reduced GPX1 enzyme activity.

sources.name: GPX1 Pro198Leu molecular consequences
sources.notes: NCBI gene record summarizes GPX1 function and variant literature.

markers.impact: Reduced NQO1 quinone detoxification enzyme stability/activity
markers.interpretation: NQO1 rs1800566 T encodes Pro187Ser, which substantially reduces NQO1 protein stability and enzyme activity, especially in T/T carriers. Use as a detoxification/redox context marker, not as a cancer prediction marker.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Disease associations are inconsistent; the strongest claim is functional reduction in NQO1 activity, not disease prediction.

sources.name: NQO1 C609T functional impact
sources.notes: Reports strong impact of NQO1 C609T/Pro187Ser on enzyme stability and activity.

sources.name: NQO1 C609T and enzyme activity
sources.notes: Discusses decreased NQO1 enzymatic activity with rs1800566 C>T.

markers.impact: Glutathione S-transferase P1 substrate handling modifier
markers.interpretation: GSTP1 rs1695 G encodes the Val105 form and can alter GSTP1 catalytic activity and substrate handling. Useful as a broad detoxification-context marker, but disease associations are inconsistent.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: GST detoxification is a multi-gene pathway; GSTM1/GSTT1 copy-number variants are not captured by ordinary SNP-only interpretation.

sources.name: GSTP1 Ile105Val functional polymorphism review
sources.notes: Describes GSTP1 Ile105Val functional consequences for enzyme activity/substrate specificity.

markers.impact: Innate immune LPS-response modifier
markers.interpretation: TLR4 rs4986790 G encodes Asp299Gly and has been studied as a modifier of LPS/TLR4 signaling and innate immune response. Associations vary, so use only as a low-confidence inflammatory-response context marker.
confirm_with: clinical immune evaluation if symptoms warrant
markers.raw_dna_limitation: TLR4-response findings are heterogeneous and sometimes conflicting; do not infer immune competence from this SNP.

sources.name: TLR4 Asp299Gly signaling consequences
sources.notes: Reports Asp299Gly effects on TLR4 signaling adaptor recruitment.

sources.name: TLR4 rs4986790 meta-analysis caution
sources.notes: Meta-analysis suggesting no significant association with infections, supporting conservative interpretation.

markers.impact: IL-6 inflammatory expression modifier
markers.interpretation: IL6 rs1800795 is a promoter variant studied in inflammatory signaling and CRP/cytokine contexts. Because associations vary by ancestry and condition, treat as a weak inflammatory-tone context marker only.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: Cytokine SNPs have small, inconsistent effects and are highly environment-dependent.

sources.name: IL6 rs1800795 promoter polymorphism overview
sources.notes: Describes IL6 promoter G>C rs1800795 and transcriptional activity context.

markers.impact: TNF-alpha inflammatory signaling modifier
markers.interpretation: TNF rs1800629 A is a promoter variant studied in TNF-alpha expression and inflammatory disease susceptibility. It is too nonspecific for diagnosis and should only be used as a low-confidence inflammatory-context marker.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: TNF biology is broad and disease associations are inconsistent; do not over-score this marker.

sources.name: TNF gene function summary
sources.notes: NCBI gene summary for TNF as a multifunctional proinflammatory cytokine.

markers.impact: ACE activity and vascular-tone context marker
markers.interpretation: ACE rs4343 is commonly used as a SNP proxy for ACE I/D-related ACE activity differences. In core interpretation, it belongs only as a blood-pressure/endurance-response context marker.
markers.raw_dna_limitation: ACE activity is influenced by many variants and clinical factors; rs4343 is only an imperfect proxy.

sources.name: ACE rs4343 as ACE I/D proxy
sources.notes: Discusses rs4343 as a proxy for ACE Alu I/D polymorphism.

sources.notes: NCBI gene summary for ACE role in blood pressure and electrolyte balance.
